Task: Implement capabilities matrix and broker adapter conformance tests
Description: Implement the Alpaca BrokerCapabilities matrix, adapter conformance tests, and operator documentation.

mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/capabilities.py:
(1) Define a BrokerCapabilities matrix keyed by environment (PAPER/LIVE) and a capability descriptor. The descriptor combines: order type (market, limit, stop, stop_limit, trailing_stop), order class (simple, oto, oco, bracket), sizing (whole-share qty, fractional qty, notional), time-in-force (day, gtc, opg, cls, ioc, fok), side, and operation (submit, replace).
(2) Each entry has a status of PROVEN, UNPROVEN, or UNSUPPORTED, plus an evidence reference: a doc URL or paper-verification record id with date. Default every combination not explicitly proven to UNPROVEN, which fails closed.
(3) Initial statuses: whole-share market/limit DAY/GTC simple buy/sell are PROVEN-by-documentation, pending paper verification. Standalone whole-share trailing_stop sell with trail_price or trail_percent is documented. The following start as UNPROVEN: stop-only OTO, bracket/OCO, fractional stop or linked orders, fractional trailing stop, stop-price replace, trailing replace, OTO replace, and fractional GTC. Short selling is UNSUPPORTED (disabled) for initial long-only trading.
(4) Provide is_available(descriptor, environment) -> bool and require(descriptor, environment) that raises CapabilityUnavailable with the reason. This is the callable to inject into the e.3 order service.
(5) Provide a mechanism to promote a capability to PROVEN only from an explicit paper-verification record. Paper evidence never auto-promotes LIVE. A LIVE promotion requires a separate explicit operator-recorded entry.
(6) Provide a conformance helper that, given an adapter instance, checks that it exposes the broker port operations (account, positions, assets, clock, open orders, lookup by id and client_order_id, submit, cancel, activities, trade update stream).

Create tests/contracts/test_broker_capabilities.py, with fixtures and fakes only, covering:
(a) unproven combinations fail closed;
(b) paper evidence does not promote LIVE;
(c) trailing_stop with an order_class other than simple is never available;
(d) notional replace is unavailable;
(e) short selling is unavailable;
(f) the matrix is complete: every descriptor resolves to a status, with no KeyError;
(g) adapter conformance: the Alpaca adapter modules from e.1–e.4 expose the required operations, and the order service rejects an UNPROVEN combination when wired with this matrix;
(h) a credential-gated paper integration test that is skipped unless explicit paper credentials and an operator opt-in env var (for example MIKE_TRADE_ALPACA_PAPER_IT=1) are present, and that runs read-only paper account/clock/asset checks. It never touches LIVE and never places orders unless separately authorized.

docs/ALPACA.md: operator documentation covering Trading API vs Broker API; paper vs live endpoints; credential env vars; fingerprints and isolated state directories; the live authorization requirement; rate limits and retry semantics (reads retried, order creation never blindly retried); client_order_id scheme and unknown-outcome resolution; trade_updates reconnect/gap handling; the capability matrix table with current statuses and evidence; how to run the credential-gated paper verification; and a statement that mocks do not count as broker integration.

Before editing, inspect: mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/auth.py, http.py, account.py, assets.py, orders.py, activities.py, and updates.py (from e.1–e.4); the broker port/protocol and capability-related domain types from earlier phases; and any existing docs/ directory conventions. Do not edit e.1–e.4 files. If a conformance gap is found, record it as a failing or xfail test with a clear reason and in docs/ALPACA.md, rather than editing other modules.
Phase: E
Acceptance criteria:
  - capabilities.py defines a matrix keyed by environment and descriptor (order type, order class, sizing, TIF, side, operation) with statuses PROVEN/UNPROVEN/UNSUPPORTED and evidence references
  - Any descriptor not explicitly listed resolves to UNPROVEN and require() raises CapabilityUnavailable, verified by a test
  - Stop-only OTO, bracket/OCO, fractional stop/linked, fractional trailing stop, stop-price replace, and OTO replace are not available by default, verified by tests
  - trailing_stop with any order_class other than simple is never available; notional replace is unavailable; short selling is unavailable
  - Recording paper verification evidence promotes only the PAPER entry; the LIVE entry remains unchanged without a separate explicit operator record
  - Conformance tests verify the Alpaca adapter modules expose the required broker port operations and that the order service, wired with this matrix, rejects an UNPROVEN combination
  - A paper integration test exists that is skipped unless paper credentials and an explicit opt-in env var are set, performs read-only checks only, and never references LIVE endpoints
  - docs/ALPACA.md documents environments, credential isolation, live authorization, retry/rate-limit semantics, client_order_id/unknown-outcome resolution, stream reconnection, the capability matrix with statuses, and the paper verification procedure
  - tests/contracts/test_broker_capabilities.py passes (with the paper integration test skipped) without network access or credentials

# AGENTS.md

## Purpose

This repository is operated by an autonomous multi-agent system (abracapocus_2).
All agents must follow these rules when modifying the codebase.

---

## Core Principles

- Minimal blast radius: only modify what is required for the task
- Deterministic verification: all changes must be verifiable via code (tests, compile, scripts)
- No architecture drift: do not introduce new frameworks or major design changes unless explicitly required
- No unrelated refactors
- All changes must be reproducible from a clean clone

---

## Project Structure

- docs/ → design, plans, architecture constraints
- plans/ → master plans
- phases/ → phase definitions
- tasks/ → executable task documents
- backends/ → CLI backend adapters
- agents/ → specialist agents
- runtime/ → orchestration, routing, state
- reports/ → execution reports (DO NOT MODIFY MANUALLY)
- state/runtime_state.json → runtime state (DO NOT COMMIT)

---

## Task Execution Rules

- Always operate from a task document when available
- Respect:
  - selected_backend
  - verification_profile
  - acceptance_criteria
- If a task conflicts with architecture constraints or phase scope:
  - STOP and report conflict

---

## Backend Rules

- Backends must:
  - execute commands deterministically
  - capture stdout, stderr, exit_code
  - not silently fail
- Do not invent backend interfaces; use existing adapters
- Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini, Claude Code should be invoked through backends only

---

## Verification Rules

- Verification must be deterministic
- Preferred checks:
  - pytest
  - python -m py_compile
- Do not rely on model self-evaluation

---

## Execution Control Flow (PERMANENT ARCHITECTURAL RULE)

**HEURISTIC INFERENCE MUST NEVER PARTICIPATE IN ABRACAPOCUS EXECUTION CONTROL FLOW.**

Abracapocus must not determine execution success, failure, acceptance,
rejection, blocking, retry eligibility, phase progression, or completion from
heuristic inference. A heuristic is any conclusion that is *inferred* rather
than *directly established by an explicit executable contract or a concrete
runtime fact*.

Runtime status is derived ONLY from concrete, mechanically observable facts:

1. The backend process exit code. A backend that exits `0` (with no hard
   write-policy violation) is a successful execution.
2. Objectively observed hard write-policy violations (changed paths outside the
   declared allowed write paths).
3. Explicit operator-authored commands (task/phase verification the plan
   explicitly contains). Their raw results are reported, kept DISTINCT from
   backend execution status.
4. Objective orchestrator failures with direct evidence (backend could not
   launch, required document could not be parsed, subprocess infrastructure
   failed).

**Verification results are observational and must not rewrite backend execution
status.** A verifier returning non-zero must NEVER, by itself, turn a
successful backend execution into unverified, stop a phase, or trigger an
automatic rerun. Verification is the result of a command, not authority to
rewrite history.

**Execution control:** Task-local problems (non-zero exit, timeout,
write-policy violation, frame failure, backend launch failure) produce
acceptance status ``"unverified"`` with truthful evidence preserved. They
MUST NOT stop sibling tasks, later phases, or the plan. Only operator
cancellation (SIGINT/SIGTERM/dashboard cancel) may terminate a run
(acceptance status ``"interrupted"``). Dependencies are ordering constraints,
not acceptance gates — any terminal attempt outcome satisfies a dependency
edge. The status ``"failed"`` is banned from acceptance output.

Do NOT reintroduce -- under any name, feature flag, "advisory" wrapper, or
compatibility mode -- context completeness/sufficiency scoring, change or
architecture assessment used as a gate, intent/scope matching, reconciliation
gates, no-progress judgments, confidence/risk scores, model/LLM/reviewer
judgments over status, shadow/adaptive/secondary-verification gates, or
heuristic retry/failure-classification control flow. Failure classification may
only *summarize* an already-established concrete failure; it must never create
one. Retries are permitted only for explicitly defined mechanical backend
failures. Future agents must not add these systems back.

---

## Git Rules

- Do not commit:
  - runtime_state.json
  - reports/
  - logs/
  - virtual environments
- Do not modify .gitignore unless required by task
- Do not create excessive commits; prefer grouped logical commits

---

## Allowed Changes

- Implement task requirements
- Fix failing verification
- Update relevant tests
- Improve documentation tied to the task

---

## Forbidden Changes

- Changing architecture without explicit instruction
- Adding dependencies without justification
- Modifying unrelated files
- Deleting important files
- Bypassing verification

---

## Planning Rules

- Plans are multi-phase
- Completed sections are immutable
- Remaining sections may be updated
- Tasks must align with:
  - project brief
  - architecture constraints
  - active phase

---

## Reporting

- All executions must produce structured reports
- Reports must include:
  - changed files
  - verification results
  - assessment

---

## Behavior

- Do not ask unnecessary questions
- Do not stall execution
- Do not perform broad scans unless required
- Prefer direct action over analysis

---

## Priority Order

This ordering guides *implementation decisions* only. It does NOT make
verification an acceptance authority: verification results are observational
(see "Execution Control Flow"), and never override a concrete backend
execution result.

1. Architecture constraints
2. Task definition
3. Verification results (observational signal, not acceptance authority)
4. Plan guidance

If conflicts occur, follow this order.

## What was implemented

**`mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/capabilities.py`**
- `CapabilityDescriptor`: frozen 6-axis descriptor (order type × class × sizing × TIF × side × operation) with strict validation/normalization.
- `CapabilityStatus` (`PROVEN`/`UNPROVEN`/`UNSUPPORTED`) + `CapabilityEvidence` (kind `documentation`/`paper_verification`/`operator_record`, reference, date).
- `BrokerCapabilities`: complete fail-closed matrix — unlisted combos resolve to `UNPROVEN`, never `KeyError`. `is_available()` / `require()` (raises `CapabilityUnavailable` with status + evidence reason). Initial doc-PROVEN set: whole-share market/limit simple DAY/GTC buy/sell submit + standalone whole-share trailing-stop sell submit (PAPER via doc evidence, LIVE via explicit operator record `OP-ALPACA-DOC-2026-001`).
- Structural `UNSUPPORTED` (never promotable): `short` side, non-`simple` trailing-stop, notional replace.
- `record_paper_verification()` promotes only PAPER, returns a new matrix, never touches LIVE or the input. `with_live_promotion()` requires `operator_record` evidence.
- `as_legacy_checker(env)` bridges string capability names into the e.3 order service (`capability_check`); unknown names fail closed.
- `check_adapter_conformance()` checks one adapter or a collection of services against the 12 required operations (tolerates both `get_order_by_client_order_id` and the port's `get_order_by_client_id` naming).

**`tests/contracts/test_broker_capabilities.py`** — covers (a) fail-closed UNPROVEN incl. OTO/bracket/OCO/replace/fractional-GTC, (b) paper-doesn't-promote-LIVE + input immutability, (c) non-simple trailing never available (promotion refused), (d) notional replace (240 combos), (e) short selling, (f) full 4,320-entry completeness sweep, (g) conformance on fakes/collections plus e.1–e.4 module exposure plus order-service wired reject/accept, (h) `@pytest.mark.paper` read-only IT (account/clock/AAPL asset) skipped without `MIKE_TRADE_ALPACA_PAPER_IT=1` + paper creds, never touching LIVE. The missing unified adapter is recorded as a strict `xfail`, also documented.

**`docs/ALPACA.md`** — Trading vs Broker API, paper/live endpoints, credential env vars (no fallback), fingerprints + isolated state, live authorization, retry semantics (reads retried, mutations single-shot + unknown-outcome via `client_order_id`), stream reconnect/gap reconciliation, matrix table with statuses/evidence, promotion workflow, paper verification procedure, and the mocks-don't-count statement.
